turns.prompt_text: how long would you have to use a e-cigarettes before damage occurs
turns.response_html:
Damage can occur after just one use. While long-term diseases like COPD or cancer may take years to develop, studies show that a single session can cause immediate changes in blood flow, airway resistance, and cellular inflammation.

Timeline of Damage

  • Minutes to Hours: Increased heart rate, blood pressure, and lung irritation. Some rare cases of acute lung injury (EVALI) have been reported within hours of first-time use.
  • 3 Days: Animal studies indicate that significant lung inflammation and oxidative stress can occur in as little as three days.
  • Weeks to Months: Frequent users may develop chronic cough, wheezing, or worsening of existing conditions like asthma.
  • Years: Potential for permanent scarring (like "popcorn lung"), cardiovascular disease, and irreversible lung damage.

Because e-cigarettes are relatively new, the exact duration required for catastrophic "long-term" damage in humans is still being studied, but biological harm begins almost immediately upon inhalation.
